title: Maximum Rows Covered by Columns
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix and an integer numSelect, select exactly numSelect distinct columns to maximize the number of covered rows.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix and an integer numSelect, select exactly numSelect distinct columns to maximize the number of covered rows. A row is covered if all its 1's are in the selected columns or if the row has no 1's. Return the maximum number of rows covered.
constraints: Select exactly num_select distinct matrix columns.
A row is covered when every 1 in that row lies in a selected column; an all-zero row is always covered.
Return the greatest number of rows covered by one selection.
hints: Encode each row’s one-columns as a bitmask.
Enumerate column masks containing exactly num_select bits.
A row is covered precisely when row_mask & selected equals row_mask.
Every legal selection is enumerated, and the subset test exactly matches coverage, so the best count is optimal.
editorial: Every legal selection is enumerated, and the subset test exactly matches coverage, so the best count is optimal.

tests.explanation: Selecting columns 0 and 2 covers the zero row and the two rows whose ones are confined to those columns, giving three.
Either single column covers exactly one row, so the maximum is one.
